findings.evidence: GLn/CosetDecomposition.lean:128-132 (`def unitriSL`, no `@[expose]`; `coe_unitriSL ... := (rfl)`) and :136-142 (`upperTriGL` / `upperTriGL_def := (rfl)`); StabConjugation.lean:52-74 is the same shape for an `Equiv`-valued def, with the comment "`(rfl)` rather than `rfl`: the equivalences are not `@[expose]`, so the parentheses opt out of exporting the definitional equality that this lemma exists to replace."; PolynomialRing/Basic.lean:98-100 repeats it.
findings.fix: Drop both `@[expose]` attributes and prove the four/five characteristic lemmas with `:= (rfl)` instead of `:= rfl` (lines 56, 72, 76, 87, 91), matching the idiom the repo already uses.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `upperTriEntriesEquiv` (line 66) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin` (line 81) over-exposes both bodies. The stated reason — "the characteristic simp lemmas above cannot be proved without it" — is false: the lemmas are in the same module, where the body is visible regardless of `@[expose]`.

findings.evidence: GLn/CosetDecomposition.lean:106-108 `unitriMat_apply_lt ... : unitriMat B i j = (B ⟨(i, j), h⟩ : ℕ)` and :152-156 `upperTriGL_apply_lt ... = (a i : ℚ) * (B ⟨(i, j), h⟩ : ℕ)` — anonymous constructor, not `default`. Mathlib's `Unique.eq_default` (Mathlib/Logic/Unique.lean:110) is not `@[simp]`, so nothing joins the two normal forms automatically.
findings.fix: Quantify the `.val` forms over an arbitrary index, e.g. `@[simp] lemma upperTriEntriesEquiv_symm_apply_val (b) (q : {ij : Fin 2 × Fin 2 // ij.1 < ij.2}) : (((upperTriEntriesEquiv a).symm b q : Fin _) : ℕ) = (b : ℕ) := by rw [Subsingleton.elim q default]; rfl`, and likewise for `upperTriEntriesEquivFin_symm_val`. Staying at `ℕ` avoids the dependent-index rewrite, and `default_indexPair_val` can then be dropped.
findings.issue: `upperTriEntriesEquiv_symm_apply_default` (76) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin_symm_val` (91) are stated only at the literal argument `default`, so they never fire on `(equiv.symm b) ⟨(0,1), h⟩` — the spelling produced by `unitriMat_apply_lt` and `upperTriGL_apply_lt`, the only consumers this file exists to feed. `default_indexPair_val` (56) does not bridge them either: it is a `.val` equation whose LHS occurs only inside the dependent fibre index `Fin (a q.val.2 / a q.val.1)`, where rewriting fails the motive check.

findings.evidence: grep for `!![1,` across TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing returns only the two docstring occurrences in this file (lines 19, 80); no declaration produces the matrix.
findings.fix: Add the interaction lemma, e.g. `lemma coe_upperTriGL_symm (hp : 0 < p) (b : Fin p) : (upperTriGL ((upperTriEntriesEquivFin p).symm b) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℚ) = !![1, (b : ℚ); 0, (p : ℚ)]`; otherwise remove the claim from both docstrings.
findings.issue: The module docstring (19) and `upperTriEntriesEquivFin`'s docstring (79-80) both assert that `upperTriGL` at these entries "runs over the classical `!![1, b; 0, p]`", and the PR calls this "the only adapter the level-N Hecke port still needs", but no lemma states it. A consumer matching AINTLIB's `T_p_upper p hp b = !![1, b; 0, p]` must re-derive the matrix from `upperTriGL_apply_lt`/`_diag`/`_eq_zero_of_lt` plus a positivity side condition `∀ i, 0 < ![1, p] i`.

summary: Both new defs carry @[expose] on a justification the repo's own idiom contradicts, and all five characteristic lemmas use bare `rfl` instead of `(rfl)`, exporting the defeq the lemmas exist to replace. The symm/val lemmas are stated only at `default`, so they do not fire on the `B ⟨(0,1), h⟩` spelling that every entrywise lemma in the imported file produces, and the advertised `!![1, b; 0, p]` identification has no lemma.
